title: Rotting Oranges
statement: 0 = empty, 1 = fresh orange, 2 = rotten orange. Each minute, every fresh orange adjacent (4 directions) to a rotten one becomes rotten. Return the minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if some can never rot.

large_tests.gen_code:
def gen():
    g = [[1] * 300 for _ in range(300)]
    g[0][0] = 2
    return [g]

hints.1_question: Rotting spreads one layer per minute, from ALL rotten oranges at the same time. Which traversal models that?
hints.2_nudge: Multi-source BFS: start with every rotten orange in the queue, spread to fresh neighbours, and track the minute. If any fresh orange remains at the end, return -1.
hints.3_big_hint: Queue all 2s with time 0, count fresh. BFS marking neighbours rotten with time + 1, decrementing fresh. Return -1 if fresh > 0 else the last time.

known_bugs.name: counts one extra minute
known_bugs.code:
def orangesRotting(grid):
    R, C = len(grid), len(grid[0]) if grid else 0
    level = [(i, j) for i in range(R) for j in range(C) if grid[i][j] == 2]
    fresh = sum(row.count(1) for row in grid)
    minutes = 0
    while level:
        minutes += 1
        nxt = []
        for r, c in level:
            for dr, dc in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
                nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                if 0 <= nr < R and 0 <= nc < C and grid[nr][nc] == 1:
                    grid[nr][nc] = 2
                    fresh -= 1
                    nxt.append((nr, nc))
        level = nxt
    return -1 if fresh else minutes
known_bugs.followup: If there are no fresh oranges at all, how many minutes should it take, and how many does your loop count?
